bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42506975 (dnsmasq): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_util [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42506975
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness reaches `hash_questions()` with a DNS-sized byte buffer in `data,size` and a separate 76-byte heap string `t2` allocated by the harness. `hash_questions()` treats the packet header's attacker-controlled `qdcount` as the number of questions to parse and calls `extract_name()` with `name == t2`. Inside `extract_name()`, each label byte from the packet is copied into `name` while the code only bounds-checks the packet cursor and the packet-derived cumulative name length against `MAXDNAME`; it never checks that the destination buffer is actually `MAXDNAME` bytes long. For the crashing packet, the accepted question path writes one byte past the 76-byte `t2` allocation at `rfc1035.c:106`, matching the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1` in `extract_name` reached from `hash_questions`.

source.description: Source. `hash_questions()` first consumes attacker-controlled DNS packet state as a vulnerability-relevant parser decision by converting the packet header's `qdcount` into the loop bound that determines whether question-name extraction will run.
source.value_from: The fuzz target passes the remaining attacker-controlled bytes to `hash_questions(data, size, t2)`, so `header->qdcount` comes directly from the witness packet. The saved crash stack confirms this parser path reaches `hash_questions` immediately before `extract_name`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. While extracting a DNS question name into `name`, `extract_name()` stores the next label byte through `cp`. On the saved run, this write lands exactly 0 bytes past the 76-byte heap region allocated for `t2`.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `/src/dnsmasq/src/rfc1035.c:106:11 in extract_name`, and states the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 76-byte region allocated by `get_null_terminated` in `fuzz_header.h:47`.

root_cause.code: namelen += l + 1; if (namelen >= MAXDNAME) return 0; if (!CHECK_LEN(header, p, plen, l)) return 0;
root_cause.description: Root cause. `extract_name()` validates only the packet-derived cumulative domain length against `MAXDNAME` and the source cursor against `plen`. It assumes the caller supplied a destination buffer large enough for any accepted name, but it never checks whether `cp` still fits inside the actual `name` object passed by the caller.
root_cause.note: On this path the caller supplies `t2`, a 76-byte heap buffer, not a `MAXDNAME`-sized workspace. A packet name shorter than `MAXDNAME` but longer than 75 bytes therefore passes these guards and still overruns `t2` when copied.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where attacker-controlled packet header state becomes the question-parser loop bound that drives whether `extract_name()` is entered on the crashing path.

parser_admitted.description: The witness leaves more than a DNS header's worth of bytes in `data,size`, so the fuzz target admits those bytes to the DNS helpers instead of skipping the packet-processing block.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness allocates a 76-byte heap string `t2` from attacker-controlled bytes and later passes the remaining bytes as a DNS packet to `hash_questions()` with `t2` as the destination name buffer.
`hash_questions()` interprets the packet header, uses `qdcount` to enter the question loop, and dispatches DNS name extraction with `name == t2`.

`extract_name()` accepts a long enough label sequence because it checks only packet bounds and `MAXDNAME`, then copies label bytes into the undersized 76-byte destination until `cp` writes one byte past the heap allocation.

fine_trace.note: Materializes 75 attacker-controlled bytes into heap string `t2` and appends a NUL, producing the 76-byte region later named by ASan as the overwritten allocation.

fine_trace.code: if (size > sizeof(struct dns_header)) { hash_questions(data, size, t2);
fine_trace.note: Control reaches the DNS helper only when enough attacker bytes remain to look like a DNS packet. On the witness run this gate is taken and `hash_questions()` receives the remaining bytes as `header, plen` plus the 76-byte `t2` buffer as `name`.

fine_trace.code: unsigned char *p = (unsigned char *)(header+1); ... for (q = ntohs(header->qdcount); q != 0; q--)
fine_trace.note: `hash_questions()` sets `p` to the first byte after the DNS header and converts attacker-controlled `header->qdcount` into loop counter `q`, determining whether question-name parsing will run.

For each admitted question, `hash_questions()` passes the packet cursor and the caller-supplied destination buffer unchanged into `extract_name()`. Here `name` still aliases the 76-byte `t2` allocation from step 1.

fine_trace.code: namelen += l + 1; if (namelen >= MAXDNAME) return 0; if (!CHECK_LEN(header, p, plen, l)) return 0;
fine_trace.note: When the next label length `l` is read from the attacker-controlled packet, the function updates cumulative `namelen` and checks only two conditions: the copied DNS name must stay below `MAXDNAME` and the source bytes must stay within `plen`. There is no guard relating `cp` to the real size of `name`, so a packet name longer than 75 bytes still remains admissible.

Sink. The accepted label byte `c` is written through `cp` into the caller buffer. On the crashing iteration, `cp` has advanced to the first byte past the 76-byte `t2` allocation, so this single-byte store becomes the ASan-reported heap-buffer-overflow write.

format.name: fuzz_util mixed-input witness
format.contract: The witness must leave more than `sizeof(struct dns_header)` bytes after the two fixed-width 75-byte string extractions so the `hash_questions(data, size, t2)` call executes, and those remaining bytes must parse as at least one DNS question whose extracted textual name exceeds the 75-byte payload capacity of `t2` while still staying below `MAXDNAME` and within `plen`.

evidence_limitations: The provided dataset patch `dataset/arvo/42506975/patch.diff` edits `src/rfc3315.c` for a DHCPv6 write-after-free and does not match the saved ASan crash in `rfc1035.c`/`hash-questions.c`, so it cannot be used as fix evidence for this specific witnessed overflow.

Stage 02 is source-grounded only. The exact DNS label layout that advances `cp` to the first byte past the 76-byte allocation is inferred from the crash path and ASan allocation size, not re-derived by rerunning the PoC or instrumenting the parser.
